div.head: II Cn 3
div.ab: And we beodað, þæt man Cristene men ealles to swiðe of earde ne sylle ne on hæðendome huru ne bringe; ac beorge man georne, þæt man þa saule ne forfare, þe Crist mid his agenum life gebohte.
And we forbeodað, þæt man Cristene menn ealles to swyþe of earde ne sylle ne on hæðenedome, þæt man þa sawla ne forfare, þe Crist mid his agenum life gebohte.

And witena gerædnes is, þæt man Cristene men ealles to swiðe of earde ne sille ne on hæðendom huru ne gebrynge; ac beorge man georne, þæt man þa sawla ne forfare, þe Crist mid his agenum life gebohte.
Precipimus, ne Christiani passim in exilium uenundentur (uendantur) uel in gentilitatem, ne forte pereant animę, quas propria uita sua mercatus est dominus noster Iesus Christus.
We beodað þæt man Cristene men ealles to swiðe of eardan ne sylle ne on hæðendóme huru ne bringe, ac beorgan man georne, þæt man ða sawla ne forfáre ðe Crist mid his agenum life gebohte.
And we forbeodað þæt man Cristene men ealles to swiðe of earde ne sylle ne on hæðendome huru ne gebringe; ac beorge man georne þæt man þa saule ne forfare, þe Crist mid his agenum life gebohte.

We forbid the all too prevalent practice of selling Christian people out of the country, and especially of conveying them into heathen lands, but care shall be zealously taken that the souls which Christ bought with his own life be not destroyed.

And we forbid the all-too-common practice of selling Christians out of this land, and especially bringing them into heathen lands; but we must zealously ensure that the souls not be destroyed which Christ purchased with his own life.

Und wir gebieten (verbieten A; Beschluss der Witan ist D), dass man christliche Menschen nicht allzu rasch ausser Landes verkaufe, wenigstens nicht ins Heidentum bringe; sondern ernstlich hüte man sich, dass man jene Seelen (-le G) nicht verderbe, die Christus mit seinem eigenen Leben erkauft hat.

And we command (forbid, A; it is the decision of the witan, D) that Christian people are not to be sold out of the country all too readily, at least not brought into heathendom; but let people take great care not to destroy those souls (that soul, G) which Christ bought with his own life.
div.note: A skips a line (‘huru … georne’), as did the sources of Quadr. and the Instituta. The other MSS' ‘sawla’ (plural) is more original than G's ‘saule’. Liebermann compares VI Atr 9.
